add.text: A coat over the back of the chair. You don't own that coat.
A dent in the quilt where someone lay. You haven't lain down yet today.
The light under the door, missing in the middle. Like something standing outside.
A window lit in the building opposite, curtain half open, facing yours.
A little seawater seeping from the gap between the two screens.
A few scales on the quilt, silver grey.
A pool of water under the door, a ring of salt around it.
A crust of salt on the window glass, as if thrown from outside.
A metal cylinder on the desk, wired to the tower.
A small parchment scroll by the pillow, in your handwriting, not written like you.
The paper bag is full, its mouth stretched open, a length of copper-coloured metal showing. You put nothing in it.
A fine scratched circle on the window glass, as if drawn with a compass.
A second keyboard and mouse on the desk, a second chair beside it. As if two people work at this desk.
A painting on the wall by the bed: you, lying in the bed.
The chain is on. You remember not putting it on.
The takeout on the table has been chewed. The teeth marks aren't human.
A circle drawn on the floor; the chair is exactly inside it.
The creases in the sheet line up into a triangle.
A mark on the door, the strokes very deliberate, as if drawn with a finger.
The rain on the glass runs in lines. Count them: seventy-two.
Thirteen pairs of chopsticks on the desk, one pair unopened.
A rank table pinned to the wall above the bed. Your name is on the last line.
A shadow passed through the light under the door, tall, like a camel. Somewhere far off, a horn.
The sunset is on the wrong side. The sun goes down past the other edge of the window.
The chair cushion is pressed down, as if someone is sitting in it.
On the wall above the bed, the shadow of nine squares. Count them: ten.
The door is open a crack. Outside is the meeting grid.
A yellow sign on the window glass. Not any letter.
The lamp is yellow. Everything in the photo is yellow.
A pallid mask lying on the pillow.
The light under the door is yellow. The corridor light is white.
Two suns outside the window, sinking into a lake. There is no lake outside.
A pair of scales on the desk. Wheat on one side, nothing on the other, and it balances.
A hoof-shaped mark on the sheet, black.
A bowl of barley at the door, steaming.
Only one bowl left on the table, and it is empty.
Both screens lit, the group chat at three in the morning: 'Received'.
A small white plaster head on the pillow. The face is yours.
It is bright outside the door, as if a star had come down into the stairwell from the north-east.
The curtain is drawn. You didn't draw it.
A very thick book open on the desk, page 751.
The tall window has become a door, open.
The door has become two doors, identical.
A calendar taped to the window opposite, stopped at November 1st.
On the floor under the desk, a patch of very small black hoofprints.
Very small black hoofprints coming out from under the bed, all the way to its edge.
Many staff badges pushed in under the door, the name field blank on every one.
The woods outside have grown right up to the building.
The meeting on the screen, twelve squares, every one of them looking into the camera.
Scorch marks on the bed where sparks jumped.
One more thing on the hook: a long robe, trailing to the floor.
The streetlights below go out one after another, in a straight line.
Everything on the desk is floating, a finger's width above it.
The bed is shaking, as if a heavy drum were sounding underground.
Rings on the door panel spreading out from the lock: the shape of knocking.
Nothing outside the window. Not dark. Nothing.
Every square of the meeting on the screen is the same face: yours.
The bed is made, as if no one had slept in it. No one has, for seventeen days.
The door is open a crack. Outside is not the corridor but another room, identical to this one.
The window glass is covered in writing: answer me.
A huge black dog crouched by the desk, wet fur, many eyes. It is looking at you.
It lies across the bed, filling it, tentacles hanging from its chin to the floor.
The whole wall on the door's side is its shadow.
No sky outside the window. One of its eyes.
